 What You Need to Know About Accounting Practice Deals - From the Trenches!
Hi Sara,
The accounting industry is evolving at lightning speed, that’s not a surprise to anyone who has a pulse. 
Private equity, valuation inflation, rising interest rates—these trends are reshaping the way accounting firms are built, run, and bought.
I recently was honored to be invited to join Marcus Dillon, CPA, and Rachel Dillon on their podcast Who’s Really the Boss? to unpack the biggest shifts happening in accounting firm ownership. 
If you’re in the industry—or just curious about how these changes could ripple into other businesses—you’ll want to tune in.
Here are some highlights from our conversation:
Phantom Equity Plans Are Everywhere
Traditional partnerships? Not always the answer. Phantom equity plans are gaining ground, allowing firms to align team incentives without handing over direct ownership. It’s a win-win for firms and employees alike.
Remote Teams, Real Compliance Challenges
Remote work is the new normal, but compliance hasn’t caught up. From payroll laws to data security, accounting firm owners are navigating murky waters. We break down the common pitfalls and how to avoid them.
New Buyers Are Entering the Game and Changing the Rules
It’s not just CPAs buying firms anymore. Private equity and other non-traditional buyers are changing the playing field, and they’re bringing big opportunities—and challenges—with them.
Millennial Owners Are Shifting Priorities 
Younger owners are rethinking what success looks like. Work-life balance, profitability, and sustainable growth are at the forefront, and it’s influencing how deals are structured.
The big takeaway? The accounting industry is no longer “business as usual.” Owners, buyers, and teams are rewriting the rules.
🎧 [Listen to the episode here]
As someone who works in the trenches of mergers, acquisitions, and compliance, I love seeing how these shifts are creating opportunities for firms to grow, innovate, and thrive.
What am I missing? I’d love to hear your thoughts—just hit reply!
Here’s to staying ahead of the curve,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Business Consultant and Founder of Deal Academy
